results.summary_before: This design is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that takes two 4-bit unsigned inputs and produces an 8-bit product. It uses full adders to sum partial products, as described in the documentation. The design is intended to be tested with a testbench of varying input values, and no external hardware is required. It is a straightforward educational example of a digital multiplier.
results.summary: This design is a VGA-based binary clock implemented in Chisel that displays hours, minutes, and seconds as a matrix of binary squares. It accepts switches to select the time clock source and display mode, and plus/minus buttons to set the time. The VGA output shows the binary time representation, updating every second. External hardware includes a TT VGA PMOD, buttons, switches, and optionally a real-time clock for precision timekeeping.

results.summary_before: This is an 8-bit saturated adder that performs addition and subtraction for both signed and unsigned integers, preventing wrap-around by clamping results to the maximum or minimum representable value. The operation is selected via two bits on the bidirectional pins, with the first operand on the dedicated inputs and the second operand on the lower six bidirectional pins. The 8-bit result is output on the dedicated output pins. The documentation is somewhat thin, particularly regarding the exact encoding of the select bits and the handling of the second operand width, but the core functionality is clear.
